p: Some people turn up thinking they'll just watch. Then they see a ten-year-old fly across the swinging section and suddenly they're asking where to sign the waiver. If you're unsure about joining in, it's worth knowing that the easier sections are genuinely manageable for beginners, and the course is designed so you can step off and try again whenever you like.

Chatham is a brilliant place to pair adrenaline with history. The Historic Dockyard is the big one, but there's also Fort Amherst nearby, a Georgian fortress with tunnels dug into the chalk hillside, which children tend to find properly exciting. Next door, the Great Lines Heritage Park offers big open grassland and views over the Medway, perfect for a picnic or a kickabout.

Over in Strood, Diggerland Kent lets kids and adults drive real diggers and dumper trucks, so if your lot love getting hands-on, it's a natural follow-up. For something gentler, Capstone Farm Country Park has lakes, woodland and walking trails, with plenty of space to unwind.

Rochester is also right next door, with its cathedral, castle and a high street full of independent shops, cafés and buildings that Charles Dickens knew well. It's a lovely place for an afternoon stroll and a slice of cake once the ninja-ing is done.

Practically speaking, plan your session for the start of the day, then head out exploring when the kids are tired but happy. Book ahead in the holidays, and keep a bag with water and a spare top handy for afterwards. A good hot lunch in Rochester goes down very well after all that climbing.
